origin.title:
Before building systems,
I built my own room.
paragraphs: Since my teens, I have worked on construction jobs to help my parents: carrying flooring, mixing mortar and building spaces, on outside jobs and in our home. We partitioned our house to rent out space more than three times. Through almost every change, I built my own room.

For a long time, I lacked some of the structure I needed to pursue dreams — preparing for an international chemistry olympiad or finding a way to attend an event. Maybe that is why I love creating support for myself and for others.
My parents worked with bricks, mortar and, sometimes, drywall. I wanted to take that experience into another kind of construction: organizations, tools and systems that open paths for more people.
origin.bridge: The materials changed. The desire to build a foundation did not.

projects.name: San System — Sistema San
projects.status: Work in Progress · pilot in one municipal network
projects.built: I created San System to connect school diagnostic data to the decisions teachers make every week. I built the role-based platform: assessment imports, skill and student views, curriculum/timetable organization, lesson-planning workflows and structured teaching materials.
projects.summary: Research first, software second. I investigated how teachers use diagnostic data, then built a planning platform for a public-school pilot.
projects.subtitle: From government data to planning for every public-school classroom.
projects.problemTitle:
Plan for the class.
See every student.
projects.problem: Pedagogical planning needs to connect network-level information, the needs of each class and individual follow-up. Sistema San uses AI to automate that preparation and bring plans, mock exams and reports into one management system.
projects.caveat: This is a pilot, not evidence of improved learning outcomes or measured time savings. The teacher count is reported in the supplied overview.
projects.contributionTitle: The workflow I built, from data to classroom.

contributions.title: Research the instructional gap
contributions.text: Reviewed education research and interviewed school professionals before deciding on a product. The core question was not how to add AI, but how diagnostic data could change the next week of teaching. That informed the requirements and prototype.

contributions.title: Import assessments and make them usable
contributions.text: Built imports and processing states for school assessment files, along with dashboards by class, skill and student. Separated missing/unassessed results from learning difficulties so the absence of data is not mistaken for poor performance.

contributions.title: Connect curriculum, timetables & planning
contributions.text: Built school-role workflows, timetables and a six-stage teacher planning journey: context, available slots, objectives, session types, weekly outlines and final review. Conflict checks prevent overlapping reservations; coordinators and principals have distinct review and follow-up responsibilities.

contributions.title: Turn teaching books into structured context
contributions.text: Built private PDF upload, text extraction, chunk-based processing, status/checkpoint tracking and validation of pedagogical JSON for units, questions and skills. This prepares reusable context for planning; it is not a claim that every scanned PDF or every AI generation succeeds.

contributions.title: Close the teaching loop carefully
contributions.text: Built planning, approval and follow-up surfaces and designed the next personalization cycle: diagnose needs, align curriculum, support instruction and revisit results. Keep educator review central, and distinguish implemented workflows from integrations and learning-impact measurements still ahead.

star: Schools had diagnostic data without a practical teaching workflow.
Help teachers turn learning gaps into next week’s lessons.
Researched the problem, interviewed educators and built San System.
Public-school pilot; expansion and impact measurement remain next steps.
executive: Teachers already had assessment results and network-level indicators, but translating them into what to teach next was fragmented. My research began in April 2025 with literature review and educator interviews; San System turns that method into a practical school workflow.

A teacher can inspect class and student needs, select timetable slots, define pedagogical objectives and prepare a weekly plan for review. Coordinators and principals get their own views for follow-up, approvals and organization. The system combines deterministic assessment-data processing with structured curriculum and teaching-material context.

I built the TypeScript/Vue/Node platform and the pipeline that organizes municipal teaching PDFs into validated pedagogical JSON. The public walkthrough shows actual application screens with demonstration data. The 15+ teacher pilot is reported scope, not measured learning improvement; the full personalization loop is still being developed and validated.

projects.problem: SOEL supports public-school students on their way to academic olympiads. Sustaining a volunteer teaching organization also means building leadership, clear responsibilities, documentation and routines.

contributions.text: Created around 50 process documents, task-sheet templates, production and cross-review routines across nine teams. Organize campaigns and four partnerships so educational delivery does not depend on one person remembering every step.

contributions.text: Built four communities with 241 students, a club system and four mentorship programs. The neuroscience olympiad mentorship connected 20 participants with a neuroscience postgraduate student. Helped create Cometa Olímpico, an astronomy book, as part of the teaching materials.

executive: SOEL connects students to olympiads, research, internships and summer programs. Its four communities bring together 241 students, alongside clubs and four mentorship programs. The broader teaching work has reached 4,000 students taught — a different measure from community membership or social-media reach.

My work includes recruiting and onboarding volunteers, training leaders, designing campaigns, standardizing documentation and building the organization’s website and Node.js/TypeScript ERP. Some roles use the ERP regularly; others use it occasionally. I am preparing the next platform while improving the organization itself.

A central lesson: software alone does not solve volunteer engagement. I shifted toward clear outcomes, weekly responsibilities and leadership development, then introduced AI training to help teams spend less time on repetitive work.

projects.problem: At Tsugrowth, I work on two separate fronts. The first is a sponsorship pipeline for brand activations on cruises. The second is EVER: a retail-execution platform designed around an offline-first Android app and a web portal.

projects.contributionTitle: Three workstreams. My responsibilities in each.

contributions.title: Research and design the sponsorship workflow
contributions.text: Replaced scattered research, spreadsheets and hand-built decks with a repeatable path from candidate brand to proposal. Structured the brief, audience fit and activation ideas; encoded ship constraints and category exclusivity; kept human judgment before the final presentation.

contributions.title: Build tools, review gates & reusable knowledge
contributions.text: Built four interactive AI tools and nine reusable skills around a six-stage workflow, including a fast track. Created an intermediate document so research, ideas, comments and constraints survive between steps instead of living in personal chats.

contributions.title: Operate the commercial workflow
contributions.text: Research brands, select and refine activations, and produce decks day to day. The workflow supported 56 brands, 261 ideas, 12 decks and three partnerships. I do not claim to own closing decisions or that the estimated pipeline has become revenue; post-sale activation and renewal are separate work.

contributions.title: EVER · understand the field before coding
contributions.text: Map how promoters, supervisors and central teams work in stores. Define visits, schedules, questionnaires, photo capture, permissions and exceptions as product flows, documented rules and state machines rather than a collection of screens.

contributions.title: EVER · Android, portal & exception management
contributions.text: Lead development toward an offline-capable Android app for promoters and supervisors, plus a role-based web portal. The prototype scope covers registrations/imports, schedules, proximity-aware check-in/out, questionnaires/photos and if/then rules that create an issue with a deadline and escalate it. Offline synchronization and field validation are development milestones, not proven production results.

contributions.title: Cruise messaging & social operations
contributions.text: Developing an internal messaging/automation platform, similar in purpose to ManyChat, for influencers and social agents working on cruises. This is a separate requested workstream, not a public launch or a claim that ManyChat features are already implemented.

Create a repeatable, constraint-aware commercial workflow.
Built tools and reusable skills with human review, then led EVER’s product work.
12 decks and support for three partnerships; EVER is still being built.
executive: The sponsorship work starts before a deck: research a brand, understand its audience, develop an activation that can work on a ship, check operational restrictions and category exclusivity, and prepare a proposal for human approval. I designed a six-stage workflow with four tools, nine reusable skills and an Express Lane for faster proposals.

The workflow has supported 56 researched brands, 261 structured ideas, 12 decks and three closed partnerships. The roughly US$5M (~R$30M) figure is estimated proposal pipeline, not revenue. I design and operate the system; the CEO owns pricing and negotiation, and the national manager validates what is proposed.

EVER is a separate product in development: an Android app and web portal for retail field execution. I lead discovery, product scope and the translation of field routines into software. The intended scope is 14,000 employees; an up-to-20-user pilot is planned for November 27, 2026, not a completed rollout.

executive: The starting point was a pedagogical problem, not an algorithm: assessment data exists, yet teachers still need to decide what to revisit, which skills to prioritize and how to teach a class with different needs. I investigated how AI could support that reasoning without replacing the teacher.

I reviewed 20+ papers, interviewed eight education professionals and designed a method that connects diagnosis, curriculum and instructional context. The prototype made that method tangible for teachers; San System became the product through which I could develop it into a school workflow.

I presented the research at ABRIC, receiving Best Project in Sociolinguistics, and submitted it to FEBRACE and Prêmio Jovem Cientista. These submissions are distinct from awards. The research does not establish a causal learning gain or a completed nationwide deployment.

story.eyebrow: My story / A trajectory in the making
story.title:
Before building products,
I had to build
my own foundation.
story.description: A path through learning, choices and systems — toward public education and the opportunities that should reach more students.

portrait.alt: Fausto smiling outdoors in a dark jacket with a red backpack and event badge
portrait.caption: A moment from the journey — beyond the projects.

chapters.label: Curiosity · construction
chapters.title: A different kind of builder.
chapters.text: At ten, I could not name the career I wanted. I knew I wanted to build something new, explain it and watch it grow. Working alongside my father made building physical: carrying materials, mixing mortar, laying tiles and building my own room as our home changed. Coding, videos and management became another set of tools.
chapters.note: The construction language of this site comes from real work, not only a metaphor.

chapters.label: Practice · communication
chapters.title: A voice built through practice.
chapters.text: Speaking confidently did not come easily. I studied speeches in Portuguese and English, practiced pacing, joined Model UN, gave presentations and taught programming. No single moment changed it all. I kept the approaches that helped and built around the difficulty.

chapters.label: Access · initiative
chapters.title: Talent was not the missing material.
chapters.text: Living in a public-school environment showed me how much opportunity depends on knowing that a path exists — and having somewhere to work toward it. I found quiet study time in the school office, studied chemistry and programming, began teaching and investigated how schools could use data better.
chapters.note: The experience shaped both SOEL and the questions behind San System.

chapters.label: Chemistry · resourcefulness
chapters.title: Find the lab. Build the route.
chapters.text: Preparing for international chemistry competitions meant looking beyond the resources immediately available. I contacted universities, research institutes and schools to find laboratory practice. The work was not only studying a subject; it was learning how to ask for access and make use of it.
chapters.note: Later, a scholarship and student housing gave me more structure and a community of people pursuing different ambitions.

chapters.label: SOEL · leadership
chapters.title: Software was not the whole answer.
chapters.text: I founded SOEL to connect students to opportunities, then learned that sharing information was not enough. Leading volunteers with limited weekly time required culture, onboarding, mentorship and clear outcomes. I built an ERP, but adoption varied: a tool alone could not replace leadership or a working organizational model.
chapters.note: The question changed from “what can I build?” to “what does this team actually need?”

chapters.label: Research · San System
chapters.title: From a question to a school workflow.
chapters.text: I investigated how AI could help teachers turn diagnostic learning data into instruction, developed a personalization method and a prototype, then built San System. The product connects data, curriculum and planning while keeping educators in control. It is still being developed and validated.

chapters.label: Business · what comes next
chapters.title: Keep building. Ask better questions.
chapters.text: At Tsugrowth, I work on AI-supported proposals, EVER and internal tools. I want to get better at testing a decision before it costs a team time or trust: understand the problem, build, measure and adjust. The materials have changed, but I still care about creating the structure people need to move forward.
chapters.note: IEO and IOAI remain goals. The next chapter is not a completed achievement.

overview.title: Building a voice. Then building useful things.
paragraphs: I learned to build with what was available: helping on construction jobs, creating space to study and teaching myself how to turn ideas into something useful. For years, I also worked at becoming more confident speaking — through practice, presentations, teaching and conversation.

Living in a public-school environment made the gap between talent and access concrete. Olympiads opened a path, but finding mentors, study structure and laboratory practice took initiative. I began building SOEL so other students would not have to navigate every step alone.

Today, that same question connects my work: what structure is missing? Research became San System; volunteer leadership taught me that software is not always the answer; Tsugrowth is where I apply those lessons to business workflows and products.
